newsitem.title: UK: N. Tonks repeats call to reject FKI offer.
newsitem.headline: N. Tonks repeats call to reject FKI offer.

text.p: British property development firm Newman Tonks Group Plc on Monday again urged shareholders to reject the takeover offer by engineering group FKI Plc.
"The prospects for Newman Tonks are now excellent and the board reiterates that the offer (by FKI) is wholly inadequate," Newman Tonks said in a statement.

Earlier on Monday FKI said it had got acceptances for some 26.2 million shares representing 20.45 percent shareholding in property development firm as part of its 195.7 million stg hostile bid launched last December.
Newman Tonks said its management had "successfully repositioned and refocused" the group.

"It is now an international business poised to benefit from its expansion into continental Europe and the USA as well as from the expected upturn in construction markets, particularly in the UK," it said.
Newman has always urged its shareholders to reject the offer saying the bid failed to reflect its future prospects.

The company said the board will be writing to shareholders to provide further information about the group's business and prospects inluding a profit estimate and dividend forecast for the year ended December 31, 1996.
FKI has extended its offer until 1500 GMT on January 24.
"... A profit estimate for 1996 will be released before shareholders need take any action." Newman's chief executive Geoff Gahan said.
